sections.summary: Dynamic retargeting lets advertisers re-engage Pinterest users who previously visited their site or left items in a basket.

claims.text: Dynamic retargeting on Pinterest reaches people who have already visited your site or who have items sitting in their shopping basket.

claims.text: It can retarget exact products or similar products to those a person engaged with while browsing on Pinterest.

sections.summary: The Pinterest tag sends product-level events, and a lookback window decides who qualifies for retargeting.

claims.text: The Pinterest tag tracks conversion events (Checkout, Addtocart, Pagevisit) and passes back product IDs that must match catalogue product IDs.

evidence.locator: **Select a lookback timeframe** by choosing a start and end date and an event type to focus on

claims.text: Retargeting is focused by a lookback timeframe made up of a start and end date and an event type to focus on.

claims.text: The lookback value defines who is targeted: with a 7-day window, you target anyone who engaged with a Products page in the past 7 days.

sections.summary: Best suited to advertisers with an active catalogue, tag events, and sufficient recent site activity.

claims.text: Use it when you want to re-engage shoppers who visited your site or abandoned a basket with the exact or similar products they viewed.

claims.text: Do not rely on it when your traffic volume is low: you must meet the required number of Pagevisit and Addtocart events in the last seven days before dynamic retargeting can run.

relationships.name: Website Custom Audiences
relationships.difference: Website Custom Audiences reaches people who visited the advertiser's site using Meta pixel tracking to build a targeted audience for a targeted ad; Pinterest dynamic retargeting additionally ties catalogue product IDs to tag events so exact or similar products can be retargeted on Pinterest.
relationships.context: Reaching previous website visitors with product-focused ads on Meta vs Pinterest
